evidence.text: BofA (Wamsi Mohan, 2026-10-21) models FQ1 revenue $4.22B, EPS $4.29 and GM 56.4%, above both the company guide ($4.1B / $4.00 / 55-56%) and consensus ($4.16B / $4.11), says its industry checks show no pricing pressure from the Toshiba expansion and calls hyperscaler pricing talks 'constructive'; it cut its exabyte growth assumption to 21% y/y while lifting price/TB to +24% y/y.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: WDC beat in each of the last three prints and fell -10.1% (Jan-26), -0.7% (Apr-26) and -13.0% (Aug-26; EPS $3.56 vs $3.31, revenue $3.75B vs $3.70B, guide above consensus). Beats on the reported quarter have been sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a published sell-side note, so the number is partly priced; the stock rose +3.9% on it on 10-21 and then gave all of that back and more (~-7%) on 10-22 before the print, so the market is not paying for a beat - a priced beat would show the stock holding the 10-21 gain and skew easing, not +11 vol points of put demand.
evidence.independence: Same direction from the company's own guide-vs-consensus gap (guide midpoint $4.1B below a ~$4.15B consensus; last quarter's revenue beat the guide midpoint) in the 8-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106040/000162828026053305/a4ex991-pressreleaseq426.htm.

evidence.text: CFO Kris Sennesael at Citi's TMT conference (2026-09-09, mid-quarter): GM in the mid-50s 'should keep rising' with no ceiling he can see, price/TB up 18-19% y/y last quarter with 'a little bit more room there to grow', the vast majority of calendar-2027 volume already under LTAs, 52-week lead times, revenue gated by supply not demand.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: Q1 guide was above revenue consensus but GM 55-56% was ~200bp below Seagate's mid-57% and the stock fell -13.0%; the guide's margin line, not revenue, is what was punished last time.
evidence.why_not_priced: Said publicly six weeks ago, but since then the stock has fallen ~50% from its high on a supply-side (Toshiba) scare that does not touch calendar-2027 pricing already set in LTAs; if the market were pricing a continued GM ramp into the December-quarter guide, the stock would not be at the April low with puts bid.
evidence.independence: BofA expects December-quarter GM approaching 59% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html); Wells Fargo sees a path to 60-65% GM (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/wdc-stx-stocks-headed-for-third-straight-weekly-loss-wells-fargo-slashes-targets-but-sees-opportunity/cZxKGWBRBs9).

evidence.text: At the same Citi conference the CFO flagged near-term DRAM and NAND cost headwinds - a component-cost item that could cap the GM step in the December-quarter guide while memory prices are rising.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August print was sold on a margin guide that disappointed versus Seagate (-13.0%).
evidence.why_not_priced: No preview or sell-side note found mentions memory BOM cost for WDC; consensus GM views (BofA 56.4%, ~59% Dec-Q) assume clean expansion. If priced, previews would carry a GM haircut for memory costs. DRAM/NAND are a small share of an HDD bill of materials, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: Same document as the finding above (one transcript read two ways, one bullish line and one bearish line); no second source for the cost headwind found.

evidence.text: Exabyte shipments are supply-capped below the 25% target: Q4 FY26 231EB +22% y/y (CFO: 22-23%), and BofA cut its FQ1 exabyte growth estimate to 21%; volume, not price, is the line that can disappoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Exabyte growth below the 25% target was part of the August print that fell -13.0%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Known since August; the specific risk is that sub-25% bit growth on the call reads as share loss to Seagate's HAMR at a moment when the market is worried about new supply - the market has priced supply risk from Toshiba but the BofA cut to 21% is two days old.
evidence.independence: BofA estimate cut to 21% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html), a different source from the transcript.

evidence.text: The call is the first chance for management to answer the Toshiba capacity scare (Nikkei 2026-10-02: Toshiba to double HDD capacity for AI data centres by its fiscal 2027, i.e. from April 2027, ~$380M investment) with LTA news: management said in August it is 'in the throes of' negotiating LTAs for calendar 2029-2031 and in September that customers want contracts to 2030-31 but 'we haven't signed them yet'; a signed multi-year LTA disclosed tonight would directly rebut the supply-glut thesis behind the 18-22% drawdown.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has carried an LTA-signing announcement; the August print with LTA commentary but no signing fell -13.0%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The October drawdown was attributed to Toshiba supply (Wells Fargo cut targets on 'pricing power' fears; Morgan Stanley called it multiple-driven, not earnings). If the market were pricing contracted pricing to 2029+, the stock would not have re-tested its April low at $330 on 10-19 with +11 vol points of put skew. Whether a signing is announced tonight is uncertain, which is why the range runs negative too (no signing plus soft December-quarter GM).
evidence.independence: Citi (2026-10-02) said the market overstates Toshiba's impact because Toshiba depends on outside suppliers for heads and media (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/seagate-tumbles-10-western-digital-125250923.html); BofA's checks show no pricing pressure (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html).

evidence.text: Reaction function: WDC fell after each of its last three prints despite beats (-10.1%, -0.7%, -13.0%), and in August a guide above revenue consensus still produced -13.0% and a sector sell-off; the market's habit on this name is to sell the release.
evidence.why_not_priced: The three sell-offs came off record highs after big run-ups (August: ~+200% YTD into the print); this time the stock is -49% from its record close, so part of the sell-the-news mechanism may be spent. Filed small because the skew already prices downside.
evidence.independence: Baseline history (sealed file) shows the same three negative reactions; same direction as the +11 vol-point put skew.

evidence.text: Expectations have been reset into the print: -22% over 20 days, -49% from the $746 record close, a re-test of the $330 April low on 10-19, Wells Fargo cutting its target from $730 to $450 on 10-16, and roughly -7% intraday on 10-22 on a sector de-rating (weak NAND/PC demand, memory names sold) that does not touch nearline HDD; Morgan Stanley called the ~18% sell-off multiple-driven, not an earnings collapse.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last five prints that came in after a period without a big run-up (Jan-25 to Oct-25) all rose (+1.2% to +10.2%); the three sold prints came after big run-ups.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price itself, so this is a lean, not a fact the market lacks; it is sized small and against a strong put skew because the option market is explicitly paying for further downside and pre-print run-ups have not predicted direction in this repo's sample.
